title: Decline curve analysis
status: gate met - AC-1..AC-6 met: a synthetic hyperbolic history generated at qi 1000, Di 0.01/day and b 0.5 is recovered exactly; a b outside the module's Arps bounds is refused with the bounds named (AC-2); a history whose best fit wants b above the maximum is refused rather than reported at the bound (SG-06-6); excluded points are listed with their reasons and counted (AC-3); the sibling tools' independent DeclineFitter agrees within a stated tolerance and a disagreement would be shown rather than resolved (AC-4); a refused or non-converged fit draws no curve (AC-5); and the same history and model give the same fit (AC-6).

dataModel.decision: ProductionForecasting owned PRODUCTION_FORECAST and its points, which record a forecast rather than a fit. RES-06's contract (qi, Di, b, EUR, R2, points used and excluded, bounded) is a different record, so DECLINE_FIT was added to the same owning module and registered. The parameters are stored on the run because the fit is what the engineer accepted: a later change to the history must not silently change a saved analysis.
tables: DECLINE_FIT (FIT_ID key, WELL_ID, POOL_ID, MODEL, OUTCOME, REFUSAL_CODE, REFUSAL_MESSAGE, QI, DI_PER_DAY, B, BOUNDED_IND, EUR, ECONOMIC_LIMIT, VOLUME_OUOM, R_SQUARED, POINTS_USED, POINTS_EXCLUDED, EXCLUSIONS_TEXT, HISTORY_FROM, HISTORY_TO, CROSS_CHECK_SOURCE, CROSS_CHECK_QI, CROSS_CHECK_B, CROSS_CHECK_AGREES, CROSS_CHECK_TEXT, ACTOR, RECORDED_AT) - a refused fit would carry its code and message and no parameters, so a refusal can never read as a result
dataModel.registration: ProductionForecastingModule now registers four types; --smoke reports 392 entity types (up from 391).
dataModel.reads: PPDM PDEN_VOL_SUMMARY through PDEN_WELL and WELL at PRD-01's grain: the highest amendment per entity, day and activity, production rows only, each fluid summed within the dominant unit it is recorded in.

implementation.authoritative: The ProductionForecasting module's DCAGenerator is authoritative. The sibling tools checkout's TheTechIdea.OilGas.Production.DeclineFitter is the independent cross-check, and a disagreement is shown rather than resolved - the feature's open question answered.
implementation.service: src/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop.Data/Reservoir/OgDecline.cs (DeclineModels, DeclineFluids, OgDeclineInputs, OgDeclinePoint, OgDeclineCrossCheck, OgDeclineFit, OgDeclineWorkspace, DeclineRules, IOgDeclineCurve, OgDeclineCurveService with AnalyzeAsync/SaveAsync/LoadAsync and the public Fit)
implementation.rules: DeclineRules states the models and fluids, the bounds lookup from the owner's Arps constants, the validation (well, fluid, model, a fixed b inside the bounds, a positive economic limit), the cross-check tolerance (b 0.05 absolute, qi 5% relative) and the determinism sentence once.
implementation.page: src/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop/Views/DeclineCurvePageView.cs (route 'declinecurve': the well/fluid/date-range bar, the model/fixed-b/economic-limit bar, the fit summary, the bounds sentence, the refusal or bounds line, the cross-check, the excluded points and their reasons, the gaps, the fitted curve and the saved fits)
implementation.wiring: OgBootstrapper (IOgDeclineCurve), OgApplication.DeclineCurve, catalog 'declinecurve' (OgModuleKeys.Reservoir), OgPageFactory, en + ar labels
implementation.projectReference: Desktop.Data now references the sibling tools' TheTechIdea.OilGas.Production project so the cross-check is the real second implementation, not a copy of it.
implementation.tests: test/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop.Tests/DeclineCurveTests.cs (11, no database) + DeclineCurveGatewayTests.cs (1 opt-in, real SQLite)

integration.database: SQLite with WELL, PDEN_WELL, PDEN_VOL_SUMMARY and DECLINE_FIT, seeded in DeclineCurveGatewayTests with a 24-month hyperbolic history at qi 1000, Di 0.01/day and b 0.5, two of whose months are recorded as zero
integration.ac1_reference: the fit reads the PPDM rows and returns qi within [999, 1001], Di within [0.0099, 0.0101] and b within [0.49, 0.51], R2 1.000 at 22 used points with EUR above zero in bbl
integration.ac3_exclusions: the two zero-volume months are excluded with the reason 'a rate of zero or less cannot be fitted on a log scale', counted (22 used, 2 excluded) and printed one per line
integration.ac4_cross_check: the tools' DeclineFitter is fitted to the same rows and agrees; the saved row stores CROSS_CHECK_AGREES='Y' with its qi and b
integration.ac5_no_curve: a range of three months is refused with decline-too-few-points naming the minimum of 6, and a well with no history is refused with the same code rather than fitted to another well's rows
integration.ac2_bounds: a fixed b of 1.5 or -0.1 is refused with decline-b-outside-bounds naming the 0 to 1 range
integration.sg066_unbounded: a history generated at b 1.5 is refused with decline-fit-unbounded and the message that the data wants a b above the configured maximum, with no parameters and no curve
integration.history_unavailable: dropping DECLINE_FIT makes LoadAsync return a workspace with HistoryFailed true, and new fits are still allowed

gates.AC-1 A synthetic history with known para: pass - the unit test generates 24 monthly points from q = 1000 / (1 + 0.5 x 0.01 x t)^(1/0.5) and the fit returns qi 1000.0000, Di 0.010000/day, b 0.500000 with R2 1.000000; the gateway test recovers the same parameters from real PPDM rows within 1% on qi, 1% on Di and 0.01 on b.
gates.AC-2 b outside the configured bounds is: pass - the bounds are the module's own ForecastAlgorithmConstants.ArpsBdfMinB/ArpsBdfMaxB (0 and 1), a fixed b outside them is refused with decline-b-outside-bounds naming both, and an automatic fit that the data pushes to the upper bound is refused with decline-fit-unbounded rather than reported at the bound (SG-06-6).
gates.AC-3 Excluded points are listed with rea: pass - a zero or negative rate is excluded with 'a rate of zero or less cannot be fitted on a log scale', counted in POINTS_EXCLUDED and printed with its date and rate; a saved fit stores the same list in EXCLUSIONS_TEXT.
gates.AC-4 The tools' DeclineFitter agrees wit: pass - the second implementation is fitted to the same points and compared at b 0.05 absolute and qi 5% relative; on both the synthetic and the SQLite history it agrees, and a disagreement would be recorded as CROSS_CHECK_AGREES='N' with both parameter sets in the sentence. A cross-check that cannot run is reported as unavailable and recorded through the failure reporter rather than failing the fit.
gates.AC-5 A non-converged fit draws no curve: pass - a refused fit has HasCurve false, no qi/Di/b and a CurveText of 'no curve is drawn for a fit that did not succeed', and SaveAsync refuses to keep it (decline-nothing-to-save).
gates.AC-6 Results are deterministic for the s: pass - the search is a fixed golden-section sequence over a deterministic least-squares fit with no random or clock-dependent step; two runs of the same history and model compare equal on every parameter, the EUR and the whole description.

fixed.where: Beep.OilandGas.ProductionForecasting/DCA/DCAGenerator.cs - FitCurve and the regression it calls
fixed.finding: DCAAnalysisService.AnalyzeDeclineAsync threw ConvergenceException ('Failed to converge within maximum iterations. Iterations: 100, Final Error: 1.186775E+139') on a textbook hyperbolic history at qi 1000, Di 0.01/day, b 0.5. Its FitCurve builds a basis whose second function uses the same parameter as both the coefficient and the exponent, so the normal equations are ill-posed and the step diverges.
fixed.fix: Two additive methods: TryFitDecline fits qi and Di by exact ordinary least squares on the b-transformed rate (q^-b = qi^-b (1 + b Di t), with b = 0 the exponential case) and finds b itself with a golden-section search restricted to the caller's bounds, evaluating both bounds explicitly so a fit the data pushes to a bound is reported as pinned rather than as an answer; TryFitDeclineAtB is the fixed-b form. FitCurve is untouched, so existing callers are unaffected.
fixed.verification: TryFitDecline returns qi 1000.0000, Di 0.010000, b 0.500000, R2 1.000000 at the reference history, and the sibling tools' independently written DeclineFitter returns the same three parameters to the same precision on the same points - two implementations, one answer.

noted.finding: The service records Iterations as DCAConstants.DefaultMaxIterations and Converged as true unconditionally ('Note: actual iterations not tracked in current implementation'), so its DCAFitResult could never report a non-converged fit even if the solve had failed.
noted.handling: This feature does not use that path: it calls the new TryFitDecline/TryFitDeclineAtB, whose result carries the real parameter set and whether it was pinned at a bound. The service's own reporting is left as the owner's to fix and is recorded here rather than silently relied on.

limits: There is no plot: the feature's rate-vs-time chart (history points, fitted curve, forecast, interaction handler) is not drawn, because these calculation screens still have no chart host - the same limit RES-01..RES-05 record. The fitted values are printed point by point instead.

The Monte Carlo band (P90/P50/P10 from OgForecastBand) is not produced. It is optional in the plan ('when Monte Carlo is run'), and a seeded generator would have to be wired; what is shown is the deterministic fit, which is what AC-6 asks for.

MODIFIED_HYPERBOLIC fits inside the module's soft maximum (ArpsBdfSoftMaxB = 0.95) rather than applying a terminal decline; the terminal-decline segment belongs to the forecast RES-07 builds, and the fit itself is the hyperbolic fit.
The economic limit is an input: with no limit the EUR is not computed and the page says so, because the exponential theoretical EUR at infinite time is not a reserve. No default limit is invented.
The history is read from the oil, gas or water column of PDEN_VOL_SUMMARY and summed only within one unit per fluid; a well whose rows mix units uses the dominant unit and does not convert.
Gaps are detected as more than 31 days between consecutive readings and named, but a gap is not interpolated and does not exclude points.
The feature's permissions (forecasting.dca.read and forecasting.dca.write) are not enforced per command: the app gates pages.

A refused fit is not saved: the command table's 'save analysis' keeps analyses, and keeping a refusal would let a later reader mistake it for one. The refusal is shown on the page with its code and message.
